headline: GOLD SLIDES TO $4,564 AS BLISTERING INFLATION DATA KILLS RATE-CUT BETS; SILVER CRATERS 10%
snippet: April CPI printed 3.8% year-over-year while PPI surged at its fastest pace since 2022, obliterating Fed rate-cut expectations and sending gold down $85 to $4,564/oz while silver collapsed 10.6% to $77.52. CME FedWatch now assigns near-zero odds to any 2026 rate cut, with markets pricing a 50% chance of a December rate hike.

headline: USA RARE EARTH BEATS Q1, UNVEILS $2.8B SERRA VERDE DEAL — ONLY SCALED MAGNETIC RARE EARTH MINE OUTSIDE ASIA
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) reported Q1 revenue of $6M with $1.75B cash on hand from its January PIPE, while its $2.8B acquisition of Serra Verde secures Brazil's Pela Ema mine — the only facility currently producing all four magnetic rare earths at scale outside Asia. The stock is up 114% year-to-date with $1.6B in anticipated DOC funding in final documentation.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD AND ORLA MINING COMBINE IN $18.5B DEAL TO CREATE NORTH AMERICA'S NEW SENIOR GOLD PRODUCER
snippet: Equinox Gold and Orla Mining signed a definitive all-share merger agreement on May 13 to create an $18.5B senior gold producer targeting 1.1 million oz per year from six mines across Canada, the US, Mexico, and Nicaragua. Shareholders vote in July 2026 with closing targeted Q3; Equinox CEO Darren Hall will lead the combined company.

headline: COPPER SMASHES COMEX RECORD AT $6.69/LB AS CHINA'S SULFURIC ACID BAN AND REFINED OUTPUT CUT BITE
snippet: Copper futures surged 2.4% to an all-time Comex record of $6.69/lb amid compounding supply shocks: China's May 1 ban on sulfuric acid exports, Middle East disruptions threatening up to 4.8 million tonnes of mine production, and a 3% drop in China's refined copper output in April. The metal has risen 37% year-over-year on AI data-center buildout and energy transition demand.

headline: GALWAY METALS HITS 20.7 G/T GOLD OVER 11M AT CLARENCE STREAM — HIGH GRADE CONFIRMED IN STEP-OUT DRILLING
snippet: Galway Metals (TSXV: GWM) reported high-grade intercepts at the Southwest Deposit of its Clarence Stream project in New Brunswick, highlighted by 20.7 g/t gold over 11.0 metres in step-out drilling on May 14. Results extend the known ore system and maintain momentum at one of Atlantic Canada's most active junior gold exploration programs.

headline: INDIA HIKES GOLD AND SILVER IMPORT DUTIES — DOMESTIC DISCOUNTS HIT RECORD $200/OZ AS MODI URGES LESS GOLD BUYING
snippet: India raised gold and silver import duties to shore up the weakening rupee on May 13, driving domestic gold discounts to a record $200/oz below spot — the deepest discount ever recorded in the world's second-largest gold market. Prime Minister Modi publicly called for Indians to reduce gold purchases, a politically charged signal with structural implications for global physical demand.

headline: THE DOLLAR IS SHRINKING — MONEY METALS ARGUES GOLD'S REAL BREAKOUT MAY STILL LIE AHEAD
snippet: With April CPI at 3.8% and the Fed trapped between inflation and recession, Money Metals argues that dollar debasement has reached an inflection point where gold's real move may still be ahead despite the metal having touched $4,700 on May 14. The analysis contends that investors anchored to headline dollar prices are missing the structural shift already underway in purchasing power.

headline: ONYX GOLD ADDS FOURTH RIG, EXPANDS MUNRO-CROESUS TO 110,000M — ONE OF TIMMINS CAMP'S LARGEST ACTIVE PROGRAMS
snippet: Onyx Gold (TSXV: ONYX) expanded its Munro-Croesus drill program to 110,000 metres with a fourth rig, making it one of the largest active gold exploration campaigns in the historic Timmins camp of northern Ontario. The company has completed roughly 60,000m across 145 holes with emerging high-grade zones at Argus Main and Argus North delivering broad gold mineralization with elevated-grade corridors.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD-TO-SILVER RATIO AT 55 IS FLASHING A CLASSIC BULLISH SIGNAL FOR SILVER
snippet: GoldSeek's Gold SWOT analysis highlights that the ratio compressing from 62:1 to 55:1 in a single week following the US-China tariff truce historically marks the early innings of sustained silver outperformance. The analysis argues the May 15 inflation-driven selloff may represent a reset opportunity rather than a trend reversal, with silver's structural industrial demand floor remaining intact.

headline: CRITICAL ELEMENTS RELEASES ASSAY RESULTS FROM 10,000M DRILL PROGRAM AT ROSE WEST LITHIUM PROJECT
snippet: Critical Elements Lithium (TSXV: CRE) released drill assay results from its 10,000-metre program at the Rose West lithium property in Quebec's James Bay region, advancing one of Canada's most closely watched hard-rock lithium assets. The results arrive as lithium demand for grid-scale battery storage is forecast to grow 55% in 2026, narrowing the global surplus and supporting a price recovery.

headline: URANIUM CLIMBS TO 2-MONTH HIGH NEAR $86.50/LB AS META AND MICROSOFT SIGN NUCLEAR CAPACITY DEALS FOR AI
snippet: Uranium futures rose above $86.50/lb on May 14, near their highest level in two months, as AI-driven nuclear demand from tech giants continues to reshape the long-term supply picture. Meta has signed agreements for up to 7.8 gigawatts of nuclear capacity and Microsoft contracted 800 MW of dedicated nuclear power, while Kazatomprom forecasts a 21 million pound supply deficit by 2030.
